display.title: V'Yishalcha Bincha: Why Children Ask Questions at the Pesach Seder
display.summary_short: With Nissan approaching, Uncle Yossi explains why children are at the center of Pesach and why the Seder is built around their questions.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show for Shabbos Mevarchim Nissan. Uncle Yossi explains that no Yom Tov centers on children like Pesach. In Mitzrayim, Pharaoh targeted Jewish baby boys because he understood they were the future of the Jewish people, but Hashem sent angels to catch them and care for them. Today too, the whole Seder is arranged around the child: the Mah Nishtanah and dipping karpas are there to make children ask. Asking questions is how we learn to do the right thing, so children should not be shy, and a healthy nation is one that asks and finds its answers in the Torah, the Talmud and the Midrash. 'Your child will ask', and parents and teachers should be ready with the answers in the Haggadah. And like every mitzvah, Pesach is celebrated with joy.
display.lesson: Don't be shy to ask questions about the Torah; asking is how we learn, and the answers are in the Torah.
